text: RETIRED 2026-09-04 -- DO NOT IMPLEMENT. This entry's entire P3 scope (Slack credential resolution: app_token/bot_token/team_id, SLACK_MEMBER_IDS/authorized_user_ids, the keychain services 'agent-intercom'/'agent-intercom-acp' and the _ACP env suffix, the 4-step keychain-first precedence chain, and the 8 oracle credential tests) is VOID. It was superseded by the operator architecture correction of 2026-09-04, which retired Slack completely and replaced the custom ACP broker/headless-Copilot-CLI model with the official GitHub Copilot SDK for Go. PR #13, which carried the P3 credentials deliberation and plan, was CLOSED UNMERGED as obsolete; no P3 shipment exists and none may be created from this entry. Under the corrected architecture there are no Slack credentials at all, and Copilot authentication is handled by the SDK (ClientOptions.GitHubToken / SessionConfig.GitHubToken / the logged-in CLI user) rather than by an intercom-go credential-resolution package. The binding P2 boundary decision R7 (internal/config is permanently secret-free) still stands and is unaffected. GOVERNING REPLACEMENT: docs/decisions/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-copilot-sdk-deliberation.md and docs/design-docs/intercom-go-backend-architecture.md (revision 2). The successor work is the C1-C11 roadmap in docs/plans/2026-09-04-intercom-go-architecture-correction-plan.md, whose credential-adjacent concerns are Q3 (Dev Tunnel auth, blocks C10) and H5 (permission authorization model, blocks C5) -- neither of which is this entry's scope. This entry is retained ONLY as historical evidence of why PR #13 was abandoned. Kind retained as feature for history; priority dropped to low because it is non-actionable.
